speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have been experiencing episodic cough and shortness of breath; to help me understand your condition, how long have these symptoms been occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Given the worsening symptoms after an initial viral illness 8 weeks ago, did you notice any night sweats, significant weight loss, or hemoptysis (coughing up blood) since then?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Tuberculosis (active pulmonary).

The combination of a recent upper respiratory infection followed by one month of worsening episodic cough, night-time symptoms, and exertional dyspnea in a 59-year-old female is highly suspicious for tuberculosis. I need to confirm this suspicion immediately.

REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
REQUEST TEST: Sputum_Acid_Fast_Bacilli_Stain
REQUEST TEST: Sputum_Culture_for_Mycobacterium_tuberculosis
